stops.name: Las Vegas
stops.services: Supermarkets · bike shops · post office · airport
stops.note: Western terminus. Last true metro until Durango. Buy anything specialised here.

stops.name: Mountain Springs / Hwy 160
stops.note: Do not count on it. Treat Las Vegas → Mesquite as fully self-supported.

stops.name: Mesquite
stops.note: Full rebuild before the climb into Utah. Also last cheap groceries for a while.

stops.name: St. George
stops.services: Supermarkets · outdoor shops · bike shops · post office
stops.note: Best gear town on the western half. Sort cold-weather kit HERE, not Cedar City.

stops.name: Springdale / Rockville
stops.note: Zion gateway. Small selection at resort prices. Fine for a top-up, poor for a rebuild.

stops.name: Cedar City
stops.services: Supermarkets · outdoor shop · bike shop · post office · bus
stops.note: THE HINGE. Last full-service town before the high plateaus. Freezing nights start tomorrow — this is the mail-drop and warm-gear decision point.

stops.name: Brian Head
stops.note: Between summer and ski season much of it is shut. Assume closed in October.

stops.name: Panguitch
stops.note: First reliable resupply since Cedar City. Also a notorious cold sink — a motel here is a legitimate way to skip a 20°F night.

stops.name: Bryce Canyon / Ruby's Inn
stops.note: Big general store, tourist pricing. Open later in the season than most nearby options.

stops.name: Cannonville / Henrieville
stops.note: Two tiny settlements. Snacks and drinks at best. Plan through, not around, them.

stops.name: Escalante
stops.services: Grocery · outfitter · cafes · post office · lodging
stops.note: START OF THE BIG CARRY. Last good grocery for ~285 mi. Post office here is the smart mail-drop for the eastern half.

stops.name: Boulder
stops.note: Tiny and seasonal-ish. A meal and a partial top-up, not a resupply.

stops.name: Torrey / Capitol Reef
stops.note: ~9 mi off route and worth it. Best food between Escalante and Blanding, and the last one before the Hwy 95 void.

stops.name: Hanksville
stops.services: Two small markets · gas · cafe · lodging
stops.note: CRITICAL. Load 3+ days here. Next food is Blanding, 110 mi east, and there is genuinely nothing in between.

stops.name: Hite
stops.services: CLOSED — store, fuel, ranger station, marina
stops.note: Services suspended since 2021, 'until further notice' (NPS). Older route notes and trip reports still list it as a stop. THEY ARE WRONG. Plan zero here.

stops.name: Natural Bridges NM
stops.services: Visitor centre · vault toilets · no food sold
stops.note: Potable water at the visitor centre in season, but it can be shut off after the first hard freeze. Call ahead: (435) 692-1234.

stops.name: Blanding
stops.note: ~14 mi off route. The detour is how most riders break the Hwy 95 carry. Skip it only if you left Hanksville with 4 full days.

stops.name: Monticello
stops.services: Grocery · cafes · motels · post office · laundry
stops.note: Coldest town on the route (7,070 ft). Full resupply and a warm bed both available.

stops.name: Moab
stops.services: Supermarkets · multiple bike shops · outfitters · post office
stops.note: Best bike shops on the entire route. Fix everything here — nothing comparable until Durango. Natural rest day and last warm night.

stops.name: La Sal / Paradox
stops.note: Effectively nothing. Ride Moab → Naturita self-supported.

stops.name: Naturita / Nucla
stops.note: Twin towns ~2 mi apart. Between them you can eat well and restock adequately. Last low-elevation night.

stops.name: Norwood
stops.note: Load 2 days for the San Juans. Weather here is Rocky Mountain, not desert.

stops.name: Telluride
stops.services: Supermarket · bike shops · gear shops · medical
stops.note: ~13 mi off route and a big descent you must climb back out of. Worth it only if you need a bike shop or are bailing from bad weather.

stops.name: Rico
stops.note: A hot meal on the cold side of Lizard Head Pass. Do not plan food around it.

stops.name: Durango
stops.note: Eastern terminus.
